description: Somos a equipe Kera e estamos desenvolvendo a Base Aurora, uma experiência educativa em que jovens administram uma base em Marte, comparam decisões e aprendem com uma comandante virtual fundamentada em fontes da NASA.
summary: Base Aurora is a short, browser-based mission trainer that lets young learners make the kind of trade-off decisions astronauts face. A dust event cuts solar power on a fictional Mars base, but life support still needs energy. Before seeing any result, the learner records a prediction, then chooses one of three strategies (conserve, use reserves or repair the solar panels) and watches five connected indicators change: energy, water, oxygen, food and crew exposure. The same starting state can be replayed with another strategy, so outcomes are compared fairly side by side. AURA, an in-app guide, explains each result with curated NASA references on life support, Martian dust storms, plant growth and space radiation. It turns abstract space science into a decision the learner owns: predict, decide, compare, reflect.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Base Aurora is a playable learning loop in five steps: Explore the base, Predict, Decide, Compare and Reflect. A dust event reduces solar generation on a Mars base. The learner must keep the mission alive by choosing one of three strategies:

- Conserve: lower consumption, slower food production.

- Use reserves: keep systems running by spending stored resources.

- Repair panels: restores the most energy, but outdoor work increases crew exposure.

Every strategy is viable and has a different cost. Results are shown on five connected indicators (energy, water, oxygen, food, exposure), in a 3D view of the base and in a side-by-side comparison table. A final reflection asks the learner to explain what changed.

HOW IT WORKS

- Flutter web front end (Dart) with a deterministic simulation engine: same initial state + same strategy = same outcome, so comparisons are fair and reproducible.

- 3D scene built with Three.js (WebGL2), embedded in Flutter; a CPU Canvas-2D fallback renders the same geometry when WebGL is not available.

- AURA guide: local retrieval over a small, reviewed knowledge base built from NASA sources; every explanation links back to its source. An optional Node.js backend can connect a language model with a server-side key, validating citations and recomputing results on the server. The public demo runs without any external AI model.

- Privacy by design: no names, emails or accounts. The mission log stays in the browser and can be exported as JSON.

- 16 automated tests (8 for the simulation engine, 8 for the backend). Deployed on Vercel from GitHub.

BENEFITS

- Systems thinking: one decision affects energy, water, oxygen, food and crew safety at the same time.

- Scientific habits: commit to a prediction before seeing data, then compare evidence.

- Runs in any modern browser, no install. Respects the reduced-motion preference and lets users pause animations.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

Next steps: test with learners and teachers, a scientific review of the simplified model, new missions (water recycling failure, solar particle events) and a full English version of the interface (currently Brazilian Portuguese; slides and video are in English).

TOOLS

Flutter / Dart, Three.js, JavaScript, Node.js, Vercel, GitHub.

Note: values in the game are simplified educational units, not NASA measurements.
